body: THE GOOD NUMBER: an Indian subsidiary of Japan's Ricoh, audited by a Big-4 affiliate, growing revenue much faster than its parent after moving into services contracts; the stock went from ~Rs 100 to above Rs 1,000 in 2013-15. Investors took MNC parentage as a governance guarantee. WHY IT LIED: a PwC forensic audit found unsupported out-of-books entries; in Q1 FY16 Rs 66.7 cr of them turned a Rs 64 cr loss into a Rs 2.7 cr profit; the FY16 loss was later estimated at ~Rs 1,118-1,123 cr; reports suggest the fraud began in FY14. Shares were suspended; minority holders got little after the NCLT recapitalisation. TELLS: (1) receivables and unbilled revenue rose faster than revenue (Beneish DSRI); (2) the subsidiary's growth was far above the parent and peers in a slow-growing hardware/services market; (3) Q2 FY16 results were delayed and the auditor raised concerns; (4) a ~26% free float made the run easy. TEST: receivable + unbilled days trend; ask why a subsidiary grows 3-5x faster than its parent; treat delayed results as a disqualifier until explained. LESSON: parentage is not an audit; local management incentives can diverge from the parent's.

data.good_number: Japanese parent with ~74% stake, Big-4 audit, revenue surge into 'managed document services', stock ~10x
data.test_that_catches_it: receivable/unbilled growth vs sales; growth vs parent and peers; delayed results; thin free float
data.why_misleading: out-of-books entries manufactured profit (Rs 66.7 cr in Q1 FY16 alone turned a loss into a profit); receivables and unbilled revenue ballooned

title: Hidden trap: Ricoh India's MNC parent and revenue surge
